queue.done_note: Iteration 2 (2026-08-17T19:43+01:00): was a real bug, not a styling gap -- see the log's 19:43 entry. A1's Archive button transitions document.phase to archived but never relocates the file, while specNavigation.ts's isArchived() checked ONLY the path prefix spec/changes/archive/. A phase-archived document was invisible to the tree, the picker's Archived group, and the document panel's own header badge -- full opacity, grouped as current, indistinguishable from an approved document. Fixed at the source: /project/specs now joins the on-disk tree against each path's DB phase (spec_lifecycle.list_documents) and reports it; specNavigation.ts's isArchived(path, phase) returns true on either signal, so every consumer of SpecNode.archived is correct for both archiving mechanisms without being touched itself. The fix surfaced (did not introduce) a second gap: a project whose only documents are all archived left SpecPage.tsx stuck on 'Loading...' forever (resolveSelection had nothing to hand back); added an explicit empty state. Verified live: screenshotted the seeded fixture before (bug visible) and after (icon + dim + correct grouping) in both themes via scripts/taste_shots.py, plus opened the document directly to confirm the header's Archived pill. decisions_for_user.question: pyproject.toml pins `agentweave-hub>=1.0.0`. Essentially everything in 1.0.1 lives in the hub package (the UI bundle, spec_render.py, runner_parsing.py), so `pip install --upgrade agentweave-ai` leaves an existing agentweave-hub 1.0.0 in place -- already satisfied by the pin -- and delivers NONE of the release. Observed live: a clean venv install of agentweave-ai==1.0.1 resolved agentweave-hub 1.0.0 while the hub's own 1.0.1 was still propagating to the index, and pip was content.

If 'one product, one version' is the intent, the pin should track the release version rather than a floor. A fresh install today gets 1.0.1 of both, so this affects upgraders, not new users.
decisions_for_user.cost_if_wrong: An upgrading user silently runs 1.0.0's Hub and sees none of 1.0.1.

known_debts: The test fixture's StaticPool shares ONE sqlite connection across every session in the process, so any concurrent session can roll back another's pending write. Proven: 105/200 commits lost with a concurrent poller vs 0/200 without. test_a_conversation_whose_model_changed_attributes_usage_per_turn is xfailed because of it. A file-backed DATABASE_URL is NOT a drop-in fix -- it HUNG the suite when tried; it needs WAL plus a busy timeout.

The hub suite is ~100% fixture overhead: create_app() 121ms + drop_all/create_all across 43 tables 88ms = ~240ms per test x 2130 = ~510s against 477s observed. Session-scoping the app and schema would take it from 8 minutes to about 1.
